title_candidates.title: The Ninth Legion: What the Evidence Says
Rome's Lost Ninth: Britain or the Rhine?
Did Rome's Ninth Legion Vanish in Scotland?

description:
Where did Rome’s Ninth Legion go? This 60-second evidence-led history Short revisits Legio IX Hispana without turning an unresolved record into a certain massacre story. A building inscription from York, dated AD 107–108, says Trajan’s gate was built through the agency of the Ninth Legion. Roman tile stamps trace the unit’s presence at York and other British sites. Evidence from Nijmegen suggests at least a detachment may have served on the Rhine frontier in the early second century—but it does not demonstrate that the complete legion moved there. A 2025 scholarly article considers whether events around Hadrian’s visit and a possible security crisis relate to the legion’s disappearance; that is a scholarly interpretation, not proof of a specific battle. The popular “5,000 soldiers vanished in Scotland” framing is not established by the cited inscriptions. The precise fate, final strength, and circumstances remain uncertain.
